specification.attachment_model: dynamic attachment is supported when the bus is inactive
specification.openness: The technical specification is published for third-party implementation.
specification.compatibility_policy: Logix commits to forward peripheral compatibility across future Logix computer generations.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: FlexiBUS v1 transport and driver model

physical.topology: Point-to-point host port to one device; no passive multidrop or implicit daisy chaining in v1.
physical.signaling: Separate differential transmit and receive pairs; asynchronous serial framing.
physical.cable_target: Shielded cable up to 3 m at 500 kbit/s; qualify signal integrity and period-appropriate line components.
physical.power: Power contacts/current limits and keyed connector pinout require an electrical drawing. Disk/printer devices self-powered; keyboard power is current-limited.
physical.attachment: Attach or detach only while the port is quiescent. Ground-first/power sequencing must be defined; no unrestricted live hot-plug claim.

frames.encoding: 8N1 byte transport, 0x7E delimiter and escaped delimiter/escape bytes.
frames.integrity: CRC-16-CCITT, polynomial 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, xorout 0x0000; cover unescaped header and payload. Byte order must be frozen in wire specification.
frames.flow_control: One outstanding request per device initially; explicit ACK/NAK, bounded timeout/retry, device BUSY and response credit.

commands: Printer status and bounded output blocks
Disk geometry/media generation, sector read/write and flush
reliability: Sequence/request IDs reject duplicate execution; keep the last completed request/response until session reset.
Retries of writes must carry the same identity; media changes invalidate queued requests.
Disk devices buffer complete sectors locally. Host throughput need not equal raw disk bit rate.
Report removal, CRC errors, timeouts and unsupported operations through stable OS errors.
Reset changes the session epoch. Do not silently retry an unresolved non-idempotent operation such as print output after reset; report uncertain completion to the caller.
implementation_design.performance: 500 kbit/s with 8N1 permits at most 50 KB/s before headers, escaping and turnaround; 125 kbit/s permits at most 12.5 KB/s. Keyboard polling must not monopolize CPU during disk transfers.
implementation_design.drivers: Use architecture-neutral device descriptors and class protocols. Host OS provides Z80 or ERA class drivers. Optional device-specific ROM drivers must carry explicit ISA/ABI tags; never execute a Z80 ROM driver as ERA code.
validation: FIFO overrun and worst-case CPU service latency
CRC faults, cable removal and power sequencing

ecosystem_programme.policy: Non-exclusive independently branded implementations; software and video adoption are optional.
ecosystem_programme.class_extension_gates: Plotter, modem and specialist profiles and drivers require design and qualification. Discovery metadata alone does not guarantee operation.
ecosystem_programme.governance: DRI leads software interfaces; Logix contributes hardware specifications; independent manufacturers participate. Final charter, fees and support period remain open.

specification.driver_storage: expansion device carries its driver/identification code in ROM
specification.design_goal: automatic identification and execution without manual switch configuration
specification.forward_design_policy: connector/pin standards may reserve unused capacity for later generations

specification.execution_model: system and application components may execute directly from ROM where practical
specification.distribution_model: replaceable ROM/EEPROM cartridges are used for system and application distribution
specification.upgrade_model: software/firmware can be upgraded by replacing the relevant cartridge
specification.design_goal: reduce RAM consumption and provide controlled, replaceable system images

specification.monitor_palette_control: Baseline monitors accept vertical-retrace palette commands. From NCC June 1982, explicitly capable Color Pro monitors also accept bounded horizontal-retrace commands under technology.scanline_palette_list; do not send these to legacy monitors.

control_channel.implementation: Host firmware performs selection using controller control-channel registers; monitor fixed capability ROM/straps and serializer.
startup: Read versioned capability record with integrity check and timeout
Intersect host and monitor raster support
control_channel.failure_policy: Use an explicitly configured profile or documented common safe raster; otherwise remain blank. Never infer 640-pixel support from connection alone.
control_channel.electrical_status: External drivers/transceivers; voltage, termination, connector pinout, turnaround, timeout and packet encoding remain qualification gates. No hot-plug guarantee.

specification.raster_status: Legacy 200-line targets approximately 15.70 kHz / 59.92 Hz. Mono Pro 640×400 target 26.88 kHz / 60 Hz progressive. Porch/sync widths, polarity and analog qualification remain release gates.
specification.scaling: Integer horizontal/vertical pixel repetition, including sprites. 160/320-wide logical modes can repeat to 320/640; 100 lines repeat to 200. Reject 640-wide graphics or 80-column text on a 320-only monitor; software viewport is a separately reported service. Artemis card repeats legacy pixels/lines to 640×400 for Mono Pro; never downscales 400 lines to an old monitor.
specification.palette_mapping: Explicit 1-bit and 2-bit pixel-to-output-index maps. Color indices are not brightness values. On grayscale displays map RGB palette entries to luminance; Mono I direct DAC requires host index mapping.

technologies.name: Logix common TUI and editing standard
technologies.owner: Logix / AION Software; portable CP/M extension developed with DRI

specification.portability_goal: DRI is encouraged and later assumed to distribute the TUI extension for other CP/M computers.

services.name: Layout and screen
services.description: Query usable dimensions, clip and scroll; separate document coordinates from screen coordinates.

services.name: Adaptive layouts
services.description: Compact 40-column and expanded 80-column layouts; dialogs, long names and errors fit either width.

services.name: Semantic colors
services.description: Normal text, selection and warning roles map to color or monochrome attributes.

services.name: Input
services.description: Structured character, function/navigation key and modifier events; blocking input and polling.

services.name: Controls
services.description: Fields, lists, menus, dialogs, popup windows and consistent focus movement.

services.name: Editing
services.description: Common selection, insertion/deletion and clipboard commands.

services.name: Clipboard
services.description: Explicit formats, lengths, bounded capacity, ownership and errors.

services.name: Context lifecycle
services.description: Create/destroy and activate/deactivate contexts; redraw when needed. A context describes an assigned display region, which may be the full Aurelia screen.

services.name: Timing
services.description: System timing and keyboard-repeat services replace CPU-speed-dependent loops.

specification.state_model: Per-application context state; no accidental shared cursor, selection or editing globals. Aurelia remains single-foreground; Artemis may manage multiple isolated application contexts.
compatibility_rules: Keep the same API behavior across Aurelia, Aurelia+ and Artemis.
Do not assume display stride, video RAM address, last column or direct peripheral registers.
Legacy CP/M console behavior is preserved; Logix-aware interfaces use the documented editing conventions.
Artemis implementation mediates process access to shared clipboard and display services.

technologies.name: Logix TUI keyboard commands and assignment standard

specification.status: Accepted specification baseline summarized from the keyboard proposal; implementation and conformance remain to be validated.
specification.scope: Native Logix-aware editors, forms, spreadsheets, file views and application lifecycle. Legacy CP/M console and Unix-compatible terminal sessions retain explicitly selected compatibility profiles.
specification.historical_context: Forward-looking alternative-history design at the TUI launch; later DOS, Windows and Linux conventions are design references, not claimed historical 1978 standards.
assignment_rules: Arrows navigate; Ctrl modifies navigation granularity; Shift extends selection using the same movement destination.
Ctrl supplies editing/document commands; Alt supplies menu and system actions. System-reserved commands cannot be rebound by applications.
Dispatch stable logical command identifiers separately from physical keys. Resolve focused control, active dialog, application and system ownership explicitly.
Show shortcuts in menus/help; disabled or unavailable commands report their state. Compatibility profiles are explicit, visible and never silently mixed.

navigation.scope: only after higher-priority transient UI is dismissed

editing.keys: Ctrl+X; alias Shift+Delete in text editors only

documents.scope: line, cell or record in a document; context named in UI

focus_and_lifecycle.scope: system close request with unsaved-work checks
cooperative cancellation; not immediate forced termination

behavior.selection: Fixed anchor and moving caret. Plain Left/Right collapses to the corresponding selection edge without an extra step; vertical motion retains the preferred column. Home/End target displayed-line boundaries.
behavior.boundaries: Shared word-boundary implementation groups letters, digits and underscore; freeze punctuation/whitespace traversal in conformance examples. Plain-text paragraphs are separated by blank lines; structured editors use paragraph objects.
behavior.clipboard: Copy/Cut without a selection does nothing. Cut removes data only after clipboard transfer succeeds. Delete preserves clipboard. Typing or pasting replaces a selection as one undoable operation; allocation failure must not partially destroy selected content.
behavior.saving: Report Save success only after successful completion; retain modified state on failure. Close offers Save/Discard/Cancel for modified content; Quit checks every modified document.
behavior.contexts: Spreadsheet navigation selects cells until cell-edit mode, which uses text rules. Editor Tab indents and Shift+Tab unindents; form Tab traverses focus. F6 leaves a multiline editor. Esc acts on only one innermost context per press.
behavior.overwrite: Insertion mode by default. Overwrite is an explicit visibly indicated option; bare Insert does not toggle it by default.
behavior.optional_commands: Formatting Ctrl+B/I/U is optional in capable editors. Whole-line deletion, duplication, transpose and rectangular selection remain menu commands outside the common shortcut core.
behavior.platform_limits: Aurelia remains single-foreground. Alt+Tab exposes the supported launcher/switch mechanism and does not promise concurrent applications or preserved running state. Query lifecycle capabilities on each host.

terminal_compatibility.selection: Explicit terminal profile; no selection-dependent change between Ctrl+C Copy and Interrupt.

bindings.scope: depends on terminal mode and pending input; not unconditional Quit

terminal_compatibility.flow_control: Native TUI Ctrl+S/Q are Save/Quit and must not be intercepted by software flow control. Terminal sessions may preserve configured XON/XOFF behavior.
terminal_compatibility.legacy_profiles: Optional WordStar/Emacs profiles are whole opt-in keymaps, not conflicting default aliases. Legacy CP/M control-character semantics are preserved outside native TUI contexts.

input_contract.events: Key identity plus Ctrl/Shift/Alt modifier state; text translation is separate. Preserve Ctrl+Shift navigation and Ctrl+Shift letter distinctions.
input_contract.terminal_fallback: Traditional byte terminals can conflate Tab/Ctrl+I, Enter/Ctrl+M, Esc/Ctrl+[, Backspace/Ctrl+H and shifted Ctrl letters. Advertise capabilities and offer menu equivalents rather than ambiguous shortcut promises.
input_contract.qualification: Existing keyboard exact layout, event encoding, rollover and firmware remain engineering gates; required controls are conformance requirements, not a qualified new hardware revision.

specification.goal: handle larger documents than conventional dense memory organization on constrained 8-bit hardware

specification.abacus_integration: Standalone file-based integration remains the baseline: Pulse reads and edits supported closed Abacus documents with exclusive writer ownership. Pulse 3.0 additionally supports embedded scripting in Abacus 3.0 under technology.abacus_embedded_pulse; this does not change Pulse 1.x.

specification.design_goal: maximize source portability between Aurelia and Artemis
specification.migration_model: Recompile shared application code with the target compiler and target libraries. Adapt OS-specific modules, resource budgets and assembly; binary compatibility is a separate CP/M-80 module path.
specification.strategic_role: demonstrate to third-party developers that moving from the 8-bit platform to Artemis is comparatively easy
application_structure: Separate build profiles and output directories

build_profiles.description: One Z80 binary for base Aurelia and Aurelia+; adapt at runtime and fit the base RAM budget.
Same Z80 instruction target; explicitly declare higher RAM/display requirements.
Native ERA/AIONix program with target-specific startup and libraries.

portability_boundaries: Instruction set: recompile C and replace assembly.
CP/M record/drive interfaces versus AIONix streams, paths and descriptors: use file adapters.
Banked versus virtual memory: use object handles and bounded buffers.
Single foreground versus multiple processes: explicit context ownership and shared-service synchronization.
Disk structures: serialize portable fields rather than dumping C objects.
More RAM and a wider display do not make later Artemis-only features available on Aurelia.

public_roadmap.boundary: Existing C discipline is available in 1979; the complete dual-target framework remains a 1980 product. Recompilation is distinct from legacy execution.

technologies.name: ERA1 / Extreme RISC Architecture
technologies.owner: Logix / AION Labs implementation based on future-derived blueprint

specification.multiply: iterative multiplier with radix-4 Booth recoding

specification.page_table_goal: Use compact software-managed mapping records and a 32-entry translation cache; do not allocate a flat table for the entire 32-bit virtual address space.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: ERA MMU v1

translation_cache.context_policy: No ASIDs in v1. Flush unlocked user translations at each address-space switch; retain wired kernel translations.

backing_map.organization: One compact record per allocated virtual mapping, indexed by virtual page; stored in kernel-owned RAM. Software resolves misses. No flat 4 GB page table.
backing_map.example: 128 mapped pages require 1024 bytes of mapping records per process, plus indexing and process metadata. This is an illustrative budget, not a measured total.
backing_map.kernel_access: Keep trap vectors, refill routine, kernel stack and map-access window permanently translatable; refill must not depend on an unresolved user mapping.

faults: Translation miss traps before a memory side effect; software finds the mapping, fills an entry and retries.
Writes to a copy-on-write mapping cause a protection fault; allocate/copy a page, update mappings and retry.
Unmapped or unauthorized addresses cause a process fault. Allocation failure returns a defined error or terminates the offending process according to the fault contract.
No demand paging or implicit swap is introduced.
cpu_contract: Instruction restart must preserve exact state; multi-register loads/stores need defined restart semantics or restrictions.
Kernel instructions update translations, invalidate entries and control protection.
DMA uses physical addresses with pinned buffers or bounded bounce buffers; never translate arbitrary user pointers asynchronously.
Harvest referenced/dirty bits before replacing or flushing translation entries; merge them into kernel mapping metadata.
Maintain physical-frame reference counts for shared and copy-on-write pages; invalidate stale writable translations before sharing a frame.

timing.baseline: Begin with a conservative registered translation stage and an explicit wait/ready handshake. Do not promise zero wait states.
timing.optional_double_clock: Evaluate 12 MHz MMU at 6 MHz CPU and 16 MHz MMU at 8 MHz CPU, phase-locked to the CPU clock. A two-phase translation/permission lookup may reduce hit latency only if address setup, comparison and output timing close.
timing.validation: Measure hit/miss latency, context-switch cost, DMA contention and workload hit rate. A faster MMU clock cannot remove DRAM wait time or software refill cost.

open_items: DMA interface and electrical implementation of the specified paired-bank memory organization

physical_memory_design.status: Accepted banked-memory design baseline; electrical implementation and validation pending.
physical_memory_design.physical_map_status: RAM base, ROM, video RAM, I/O and reset overlays remain to be assigned; 24-bit physical addressing is unchanged.
requirements: Independently select both full-width modules and each rank within a capacity bank; 32-bit data bus shared by selected module. Multiplex row/column addresses and refresh every rank.
Four byte write enables per 32-bit bank; defined aligned byte/halfword/word access and alignment faults.
RAS/CAS/WE timing, data buffers, refresh arbitration and DMA contention handling.
Explicit READY/wait handshake; full-width data transfer is not a zero-wait guarantee.
Capacity straps, pair matching, boot memory test and incomplete-bank rejection.
Shared module edge interface with separate board routing for selected DRAM rails; no chip-footprint interchangeability assumption.
open_items: Exact controller ASIC versus discrete logic partition and physical component counts
Contiguous physical bank decoding and reset ROM map
Worst-case loading and power with eight modules

display_memory_design.display_dram_bytes: 16384 on Artemis 128; 32768 on Artemis 256 and PRO
display_memory_design.host_access: Separate physical apertures/registers, mapped by system MMU; address numbers remain unresolved. System DMA uses pinned physical buffers and bounded card-ready handshakes.
display_memory_design.refresh: Display DRAM refreshed by card independently of host CPU/DMA. System DRAM refresh remains in host bank controller; no duplicate charge for a second system controller.

technologies.owner: AION Software controlling roadmap; developed with Digital Research

specification.programming_model: recognizably Unix V7, simplified for small RAM
specification.stable_c_abi_scope: ERA target ABI, not binary compatibility with the Z80 target.

technologies.name: Artemis CP/M-80 compatibility / virtual peripheral bridge

specification.execution: Qualified Z80 binaries execute on the Z80 guest processor, not natively on the new host ISA; OS/memory/peripheral bridging remains required.
specification.peripheral_model: the ERA host exposes Artemis peripherals through a virtual peripheral bridge
specification.goal: preserve the Aurelia software investment while transitioning to the 32-bit platform
specification.api_discovery: Return the display/input/service capabilities actually implemented by the compatibility environment.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: Z80 compatibility module and host driver
implementation_design.execution: Z80 executes the enhanced CP/M environment in its local 64 KB RAM; ERA executes the AIONix host driver. This is neither ERA execution of Z80 instructions nor a C-source port.
module_requirements: Local boot/system ROM or a host-uploaded system image
Bank/window emulation sufficient for documented Logix CP/M service entry points
A bounded shared mailbox or dual-ported transfer window and interrupt/doorbell signals; reserve its CP/M-side RAM before advertising TPA

software_split.guest: CP/M BIOS and Logix TUI/device stubs marshal requests; applications using these interfaces do not access Artemis registers.
software_split.host: A privileged AIONix driver validates guest buffer offsets and lengths, copies data and dispatches console/display, file, printer and clock operations.
software_split.ownership: Guest-visible drive images preserve CP/M semantics. Host filesystem translation is a separate explicit mode, not transparent raw-volume sharing.

implementation_design.scheduling: One outstanding synchronous guest request initially; host completes then signals the guest. Add polling fallback and timeout/reset recovery. Never allow a guest to supply an unchecked ERA pointer.
implementation_design.display: Render an isolated guest text surface through host display services. Capability queries describe that guest surface, not every ERA capability.
implementation_design.scope: Support documented enhanced CP/M/Logix API applications. Arbitrary direct Aurelia hardware access, undocumented mapper use, timing-sensitive code and unvirtualized expansion ROMs are not guaranteed.
implementation_design.qualification: Artemis PRO support remains unclaimed until its compatibility list and tests explicitly add the module.

technologies.name: LogixLAN negotiated-rate physical and data-link standard

introduced.event_name: NCC 1981 — Logix networking / Artemis PRO launch

specification.topology: active star through a multiport hub/repeater/arbiter
specification.signaling: balanced differential serial signaling compatible in principle with EIA-422-class line drivers/receivers

pair_assignment.pair_4: reserved for diagnostics or later expansion

specification.media_access: hub-controlled polling/grant; one station is granted transmit access at a time, avoiding collision-detection hardware
specification.framing: HDLC-inspired bit-oriented framing with address/control fields and 16-bit frame check sequence
specification.hub_behavior: Stream the granted frame to other admitted ports at the common rate; destination filtering and CRC validation occur in adapters. No independent per-port rates, frame-store switching or rate conversion in the 1981 baseline.
specification.station_addressing: locally assigned link address stored/configured by the adapter; broadcast supported
specification.design_goal: simple, deterministic and inexpensive LAN implementation using technology comfortably available by 1981
specification.rate_scope: One common rate across all admitted stations; one transmitter at a time. Port count does not multiply shared bandwidth. Application throughput is lower and remains unvalidated.
specification.legacy_identifier: The stable logix_lan100_link identifier is retained for references; 100 denotes the mandatory startup/fallback rate, not the maximum rate.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: LogixLAN shared-rate negotiation and buffered adapters
implementation_design.advertised_rates: Intersection of adapter hardware capability, firmware-enforced host qualification ceiling and configured cable/reliability limits. Platform ceilings are design qualification targets, not measured throughput claims.
implementation_design.selection: Hub selects the highest rate in the intersection of its own capability and every admitted station/link capability. A 100-only station or link limits the whole network to 100 kbit/s.
negotiation: Reset/start at 100 kbit/s; keep unadmitted ports isolated from normal traffic.
Poll station identity, supported-rate bitmap, host profile and receiver capacity at 100 kbit/s.
Choose the highest common candidate; announce a switch epoch and bounded idle interval at 100 kbit/s and collect acknowledgments from all admitted stations.
Drain the current frame and stop grants before changing the distributed clock. Do not switch with a missing acknowledgment.
Run bounded test frames on every admitted link at the candidate rate; resume normal grants only after every link passes.

On failed qualification or persistent link errors, return to 100 kbit/s for coordination, exclude the failed candidate and try the next lower common rate. If 100 fails, isolate the faulty port and report the fault.
implementation_design.admission: Periodically drain traffic and open an announced 100 kbit/s discovery window. New stations join only after coordinated renegotiation; admitting a slower station lowers the common rate. Discovery windows consume shared bandwidth.
implementation_design.recovery: Adapters use a timeout independent of the distributed bit clock. On lost clock/control or switch timeout, stop transmitting and await the hub at 100 kbit/s. The hub watchdog restores 100 kbit/s and a new negotiation epoch; never allow unilateral station transmission at a different rate.

clock_generation.scope: Hub clock-divider reference only; does not require every adapter or host logic path to run at 10 MHz.

adapter_requirements.buffer_policy: Local adapter RAM, additional to host system RAM. Partition transmit/receive buffers and metadata; freeze maximum frame length and IP MTU to fit complete frames before implementation. Physical RAM chip count remains unresolved.
adapter_requirements.flow_control: Grant unicast only when the destination advertises credit for a complete frame; reserve that credit until completion. Broadcast requires credit from all intended admitted receivers. Timeouts revoke stale credits; bounded queues and retry/error reporting prevent indefinite blocking. Use flow control first for receiver pressure, not automatic rate changes.
adapter_requirements.host_service: No per-byte interrupt requirement. Aurelia at 250 kbit/s has 128 CPU clocks per raw byte at 4 MHz; Aurelia+ at 500 kbit/s has 96 at 6 MHz. Validate worst-case service latency. A persistently slow host may advertise a lower configured ceiling.

qualification_gates: Cable lengths, termination, drivers and clock skew at each advertised rate
Exact frame format/length, IP MTU, buffer partitions and credit accounting
Discovery cadence, switch/ack timeouts and independent recovery watchdog
Error thresholds, test-frame counts and fallback hysteresis
Mixed-platform admission, missing acknowledgments, clock loss, buffer exhaustion and broadcast backpressure
Sustained TCP/IP throughput and CPU load on all four host platforms

technologies.name: Aurelia banked memory organization
technologies.description: AION system controller combines DMA, 4 KiB bank mapping and CPU-independent system-DRAM refresh. Dedicated sprite SRAM is accessed through video upload ports.

specification.common_ram_budget_status: Initial planning allocation; validate against firmware, buffers and interrupt requirements.
specification.implementation: One AION system-controller chip replaces mapper registers and selected decode/control logic; external clock/reset/interrupt and electrical buffers remain as required.
specification.rom_policy: Read-only code and constants execute directly from ROM where practical. Mutable state, stacks and buffers reside in RAM.
specification.video_ram_policy: CPU uses temporary 4 KiB display-memory windows or auto-incrementing upload ports. DMA uses physical source banks and target-ready video ports. Video controller independently refreshes display DRAM and arbitrates sprite SRAM; sprite storage is not system RAM.
specification.reset_policy: Initialize refresh and boot mapping before RAM use; disable DMA and clear pending ownership on reset. Warm boot aborts/drains DMA before restoring bank maps.
specification.application_policy: Installed RAM is accessible, but system workspaces and the resident Business Tools workspace reduce application memory.
specification.expansion_policy: Additional RAM uses mapped pages; an expansion does not enlarge the CPU logical address space.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: CP/M-compatible application-memory boundary
implementation_design.discovery: At launch, the little-endian word at 0006H (the operand of JMP at 0005H) points to the BDOS entry stub at the exclusive top of usable contiguous application RAM. Keep the entire advertised range writable RAM.
implementation_design.budget: Reserve 4 KB at the top of lower RAM for the entry stub and resident workspace, in addition to F000–FFFF common system RAM. These are the initial design allocations, not measured image sizes. If implementation requires more workspace, revise the boot profile before application launch and report the actual lower boundary.
dispatch: The stub jumps to common memory before any bank mapping changes.
Common code saves mapping and application stack, then adopts the system stack.
Map the service; copy caller buffers in bounded chunks while respecting page boundaries.
Restore the application view and stack before returning.
lifecycle: Choose all workspace reservations before launching the program. Never shrink TPA under a running program.
Warm boot restores vectors and the normal map. Legacy programs with hardcoded addresses beyond the published boundary remain unsupported.
Disable optional resident tools or choose a smaller TPA when networking needs more RAM; never silently consume advertised program memory.
implementation_design.extension_api: lx_memory_query returns installed RAM, TPA bounds, reserved bytes and optional banked-handle capacity. Standard CP/M programs need not use it.
validation: Exercise programs that inspect 0006H and fill their advertised TPA.
Test nested calls, interrupts, DMA buffers crossing pages and warm boot after application failure.
Stress CPU/DMA/refresh/peripherals and display together at both host clocks and process/temperature corners.
Validate hidden and expanded RAM refresh, physical DMA bounds, page-crossing segmentation, abort and warm boot.

application_memory_profiles.status: Specified initial allocation; any future budget change must preserve the published boundary for each running program.
Specified initial allocation; any future budget change must preserve the published boundary for each running program.

dma.bank_selection: Latch physical source/destination bank and offsets on start. CPU mapping changes cannot redirect an active transfer; split logical buffers at 4 KiB boundaries before programming physical segments. Reject ROM writes, unmapped banks and out-of-range lengths.
dma.arbitration: Bounded bursts with guaranteed CPU and refresh service; device-ready/WAIT handshake; video uploads yield to video-controller fetch deadlines. Numeric grant limits require cycle-level validation.
dma.completion: Completion/error interrupt, readable remaining count, controlled abort; reset disables DMA.
dma.video_endpoint: Auto-incrementing upload ports for display DRAM or dedicated sprite SRAM; target-ready backpressure.
dma.peripheral_scope: Disk/FlexiBUS DMA requires qualified request/ready or FIFO endpoints and drivers; legacy programmed I/O remains supported.

system_refresh.scope: System DRAM only, including hidden banks and expansion. Video controller refreshes display DRAM; sprite SRAM needs no refresh.
system_refresh.scheduler: Always-running timer, row counter and refresh arbitration during CPU execution, HALT and DMA; initialize before enabling RAM use. Match row count and retention deadlines to each qualified system DRAM type.
supported_populations: 48 KiB: three banks of eight 16Kx1 DRAMs
64 KiB expanded Aurelia: four banks of eight 16Kx1 DRAMs
64 KiB Aurelia+: one bank of eight 64Kx1 DRAMs

regions.description: Includes page zero and the lower application area.
Remaining application RAM, motherboard ROM, cartridge ROM or video RAM, selected in 4 KB pages.
Stable entry routines, system stack, critical interrupt code and mutable system state.

call_sequence: Enter a stable routine in common memory.
Save application mapping and stack; switch to the system stack.
Map the required ROM and data/video RAM pages.
Execute the service; use a common buffer or alternate window for hidden application data.
Restore mapping and stack, then return.
requirements: Preserve interrupt safety across every permitted mapping.
Define nested bank-call save/restore conventions.
Separate writable state from ROM code and remove or relocate self-modifying code.
Reserve resident workspace memory explicitly.
Final ROM capacities, timing and common-memory budget require implementation validation.
Qualify CPU bus handover at 4 and 6 MHz, bounded DMA bursts, device-ready waits, completion interrupts and abort/reset recovery.
Verify independent refresh for every installed physical bank, including hidden banks and Aurelia 16 KiB expansion; derive deadlines from qualified DRAM ordering codes.
Freeze package/pinout, external buffers, memory decode, bank-latched DMA addressing and simultaneous video/peripheral stress tests.
technologies.normal_map_explanation: Normal mapping describes what the CPU sees while an application runs. Mapper capability describes which addresses can change. The same 7000–EFFF switching capability exists in every configuration, even when those addresses normally contain RAM.
technologies.full_ram_explanation: With 64 KB installed (Aurelia+ or expanded Aurelia), 0000–EFFF contains 60 KB lower RAM and F000–FFFF contains 4 KB common system RAM. B000–EFFF is therefore RAM rather than a permanently reserved ROM window. System calls temporarily overlay selected pages with ROM/cartridge/video RAM, then restore RAM. The Z80 never sees all physical RAM and ROM simultaneously.

technologies.name: Abacus formatted tables and columnar storage

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation, resource budgets and performance qualification pending.
implementation_design.scope: Formatted-table tabs coexist with freeform sparse worksheet tabs. Independently implemented historical Abacus format; no dependency on modern Parquet libraries or claim of Parquet compatibility.

schema.column_identity: Stable column ID, name, declared data type and nullability; stable row IDs survive sorting/filtering.
schema.rules: Specify rounding, collation, overflow, null/error semantics and checked conversions; preserve leading-zero identifiers as text.

storage.page_role: Smallest compression/encoding unit; byte-bounded buffers and dictionaries. Group/page sizes require measurement on target RAM and disks.
storage.footer: Versioned schema, chunk/page locations and supported min/max/null-count statistics. Bound metadata memory and permit incremental access.
storage.column_pruning: Read output columns plus all predicate, join and formula dependencies.
storage.block_skipping: Skip only when valid conservative statistics prove no match; handle nulls, sort order and pending edits. Predicate pushdown evaluates filters early and is distinct from statistics-based skipping.
storage.encoding: Dictionary, RLE, bit packing and suitable numeric encodings with uncompressed fallback. Compression is dataset-dependent; no guaranteed 75–90% reduction or heavy codec requirement.
storage.execution: Stream and batch scans; bound dictionaries, query state and join memory. Use temporary disk storage or report resource limits; do not require whole tables or row groups resident.
storage.editing: Use a bounded edit buffer/change log with stable row IDs; merge pending changes into reads. Rewrite affected storage on save/compaction, update or invalidate statistics and preserve a consistent visible snapshot.
storage.recovery: Validate replacement data and footer before recoverable replacement; retain prior valid version until success. Do not publish incomplete metadata or silently skip corrupt blocks.

calculation.syntax: Abacus native expressions or documented SQL expression subset with shared type, decimal, null and error rules.
calculation.virtual_columns: Side-effect-free row expressions; track dependencies and reject cycles. Values computed on demand; persisted statistics require valid materialization.
calculation.lookups: Scalar lookup requires unique-key relationship; missing keys and duplicate keys have explicit behavior, never arbitrary first-match selection.
calculation.joins: One-to-many/many-to-many joins produce derived query tables rather than silently changing scalar column cardinality.
calculation.sql_scope: Read-only SELECT projections, WHERE filters, GROUP BY aggregates and equijoins over local formatted tables; document supported syntax and resource limits. No claim of complete SQL standard or general transaction engine.

nested_data.launch: Flat typed columns; reserve versioned extension points for nested values.
nested_data.later: Bounded arrays, maps and structs with explicit depth/size limits, expandable presentation, indexing, null and aggregation semantics; implementation milestone not yet dated.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation and qualification pending.
implementation_design.modes: Standalone offline document access remains available; embedded Pulse 3.0 is a separate mode hosted by Abacus 3.0.
implementation_design.ownership: Abacus owns the open document and file writer. Scripts use its API; no concurrent independent Pulse writer.
implementation_design.api: Bounded iteration and operations on cells, tables, formulas, queries and report layouts; reuse Pulse language/runtime semantics.
implementation_design.execution: Explicit script actions may modify documents; ordinary formula/virtual-column evaluation is side-effect-free. Define cancellation, error recovery, grouped undo and recalculation boundaries.
implementation_design.consistency: Track changed dependencies, invalidate stale caches and recalculate through the matching Abacus evaluator. Avoid whole-document duplication in RAM.
implementation_design.compatibility: Preserve standalone version checks, recoverable replacement saves and older edition restrictions. Embedding does not backport 3.0 features to Z80 editions.

implementation_design.status: Accepted implementation design; command timing and analog settling require measurement.

memory.count_register: 10-bit unsigned count, legal range 0..512; no in-band terminator consumes an entry.
memory.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta 0..255. Byte 1: bits 7..4 palette register 0..15, bits 3..0 red. Byte 2: bits 7..4 green, bits 3..0 blue. Each RGB component is 4 bits.

implementation_design.coordinates: Offsets count physical active output scanlines, independent of logical mode scaling. Start accumulator at 0 each frame; add delta before applying entry. Delta 0 permits multiple writes before the same line, including line 0. Reject overflow, out-of-frame targets and excess writes per line; never wrap. Bridge gaps above 255 with an explicitly redundant write preserving the current register value.
implementation_design.execution: Prefetch records into dedicated sequencer registers/FIFO, outside the 1536-byte allocation. Execute during blanking before the target active scanline; reset pointer/counter at frame start. Restore a saved 16-register base palette every vertical blank before replay. Line-0 entries follow base restoration.
implementation_design.updates: Single list buffer. CPU writes only with sequencer disabled or after completion before the next frame; arm validated count/base palette at vertical blank. No implicit full-list double buffer; late/incomplete updates remain disabled.
implementation_design.wire: Opt-in capability extension over the existing Control pair, host-to-monitor during the reserved blanking window, clocked from pixel Clock. No simultaneous capability readback. Proposed fixed 32-bit write: 4-bit opcode, 4-bit register, 12-bit RGB, 4 reserved zero bits, CRC-8 (poly 0x07, init 0, no reflection/xorout), MSB first. Reset command framing at blank start; specify setup/hold, turnaround and CRC failure behavior before release.
implementation_design.budget: 640x400 raster has 160 blank clocks = about 7.44 us. Target maximum four 32-bit commands per blank (128 clocks, about 5.95 us), leaving 32 clocks for guards/commit/settling. This is a qualification target, not an unconditional measured guarantee. Advertise the validated per-raster limit; 512 total entries does not allow 512 writes on one scanline.
implementation_design.commit: Monitor validates complete commands into staging registers and commits together before active pixels. Reject invalid/late batches, retain previous palette and latch diagnostic status; never update midway through an active line.
implementation_design.scope: For raster effects on Color Pro use the 640x400 physical raster, including line-doubled 640x200. Other raster/monitor combinations require their own advertised timing budget. Old monitors receive only supported vertical-retrace commands.
implementation_design.colour_semantics: Palette is global to text, bitmap and sprites at each scanline. 2 bpp still selects only four background indices on a line; 4 bpp selects sixteen. More colours across different lines do not imply a larger per-pixel index or arbitrary 4096-colour bitmap.
validation: Worst-case four-command blanking with DAC settling
All 512 records, same-line writes, delta 255 and frame bounds
DRAM refresh and host/DMA contention during prefetch
CRC errors, late packets and safe palette retention
Base palette restore and list restart without frame-to-frame drift

pipeline_contract: False conditional instructions have no architectural/data-memory side effects or associated data faults.

fault_contract: Earlier instructions completed; later instructions have no architectural effects.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

sprites.coordinate_space: Logical mode pixels; scale together with the background. Signed 16-bit X and Y; clip at screen edges.
sprites.priority: Lower sprite number wins; all sprites overlay background/text.
sprites.registers: Two descriptor banks hold signed 16-bit X/Y, enable and reserved controls. CPU/DMA uses auto-incrementing SRAM upload ports.
sprites.updates: Switch descriptor bank atomically at vertical blank. Pattern writes require scheduled access or disabling affected sprites; 1 KiB does not hold two complete pattern sets.
sprites.allocation_policy: Five sprites in every text/bitmap mode, including double-buffered backgrounds. Sprite SRAM never consumes display DRAM.
sprites.descriptor_allocation_note: 80 bytes of live two-bank descriptors within a 128-byte reserved area; 48 bytes padding. 640 pattern + 128 descriptor + 256 scratch bytes = 1024.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

logix_requirements: Preserve standard CP/M entry points, loading conventions and available-memory boundaries.
Adapt both BIOS and relevant BDOS assumptions to Aurelia floppy formats.
Keep bank-switching entry code, stack and critical interrupt handling permanently accessible.
Separate ROM code/constants from RAM state; adapt self-modifying routines.
Discover cartridge/device ROMs through defined, versioned interfaces.
Map Logix peripherals to standard CP/M console, printer and disk services.
Provide a separate versioned Logix service interface and C bindings.
Drivers use bounded DMA transfers with physical-bank descriptors and device-ready handshakes; abort/drain transfers before warm boot or reusing buffers.
Video API exposes dedicated sprite SRAM, atomic descriptor swaps and upload-port backpressure; use programmed I/O fallback where peripherals lack DMA endpoints.

implementation_design.title: BPI transactional client/server v1
implementation_design.architecture: Thin Z80/ERA clients send bounded business operations to an Artemis PRO server. Query evaluation, indexes, validation, accounting posting and transactions execute on the server; clients do not fetch arbitrary database pages.

transactions.concurrency: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.
transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

protocol.transport: Length-framed requests over TCP; bounded messages and chunked results.
protocol.duplicate_suppression: Store committed write request IDs and outcomes durably. After reconnect, clients query status or retry with the same ID; never post the same payment twice.

data_integrity: Amounts use explicitly scaled integers/decimal rules, never unspecified binary floating-point rounding.
Record currency, rounding, posting dates, account periods and unique document IDs.
Cross-module posting is atomic and produces an append-only audit record.
operations: Role-based authorization and server-side input validation
Backup captures a consistent checkpoint plus required logs; test restoration onto a clean disk.
Bounded log growth, disk-full handling and operator-visible recovery status
Plan backups and report traffic around the negotiated shared 100/250/500/1000 kbit/s raw LAN budget and measured payload throughput; slower admitted hosts limit the whole network.
